mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 0.5% compresses the risk-free rate, increasing equity valuation multiples and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 0.5% from the prior month signals inflationary pressure that triggers central bank rate hikes, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in employment (PAYEMS) and decreases in unemployment (UNRATE) signal a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint effect of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease does not produce positive returns in more than 50% of instances (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 growth > 2% and HOUST > 1000), rising housing starts (HOUST) signal continued consumer demand, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 growth > 2% and HOUST > 1000 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained industrial production level above 100 (INDPRO > 100) signals robust economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO > 100 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals labor market tightening, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE falls > 0.2pp (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: In a high consumer spending regime (RSAFS > 450,000), a monthly increase in real sales (RSAFS) signals strong demand, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS > 450000 (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in FEDFUNDS and increases in CPIAUCSL signal central bank policy responses to inflation, which typically lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to market adaptation.
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS decline and CPIAUCSL increase does not produce positive returns in more than 50% of instances (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).
